clue.text: Female in charge welcoming brief part in prank

indicators.note: one piece welcoming another takes it in, so the female and in-charge letters surround the cut-down part
brief means cut short, so the word for a part loses its final letter

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A woman in authority makes room for a little bit part in some practical joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' reads as hospitality but signals a container; 'brief' docks the last letter of the theatrical part.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank is a playful escapade or caper, which is just what this word for merry high jinks means.

clue.text: Communicate with, and about, a church

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Someone gets in touch with, and talks about, a particular church.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach someone is to contact or get through to them, for instance by phone.

clue.text: Literary group left Keats disconcerted about Poe

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the jumbled Keats goes round Poe
disconcerted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of Keats are jumbled

explanation.surface: A literary circle includes Keats, who is rattled by the American writer Poe.
explanation.walkthrough: Neither Keats nor Poe belonged to this group: both names are just letters, 'disconcerted' scrambling one and 'about' wrapping it round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey, who lived in the Cumbrian fells, were dubbed this school of Romantic writers.

clue.text: Necktie? Almost all of stuff has tax added

indicators.note: almost all of a word means it loses its last letter

parts.note: to stuff is to cram
VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: A tie that comes with tax charged on nearly everything packed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost all of' cuts CRAM to CRA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a broad scarf-like band worn round a man's neck, an ancestor of the modern tie.

clue.text: Old Harry, for example?

parts.note: Old Harry is an informal name for the Devil, and Harry itself is a familiar form of Henry

explanation.surface: A question about an elderly man named Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Harry' looks like a person, but it is itself a jocular alias for Satan, just like Old Nick.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Harry is a familiar substitute name for the Devil, so it is an example of an informal alias.

clue.text: People need each other in desolate area across windy Sinai

indicators.note: the desolate area stretches across the jumbled letters, enclosing them

parts.note: no man's land is an unoccupied, desolate stretch between opposing lines

indicators.note: windy means twisting and winding, so the letters of Sinai are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller crossing the barren, windswept Sinai realises everyone depends on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'windy' scrambles the desert's name and 'across' has the desolate area span it, splitting after its first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne's famous line says no person is self-sufficient, which is the idea that humans depend on one another.

clue.text: Plot against father, quietly, inside

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: inside places the quiet letter within the word for father

parts.note: a sire is a father
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone schemes against their dad, keeping it quiet indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot is to scheme secretly with others, the verb sense meant here.

clue.text: Relative, awfully nice, close to uncle

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of nice are rearranged
close means the end, so the last letter of uncle is taken

explanation.surface: A really pleasant relation who is near to their uncle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' looks like an intensifier for nice but is the anagram signal, giving NIEC.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member, so a kind of relative.

clue.text: Drink –- a small measure upset over girl

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed above the following piece
upset means turned upside down, which in a down clue reads the words upwards

parts.note: a gram is a small unit of weight
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A drink is knocked over, a small tot spilled onto a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns A GRAM into MARGA, which 'over' places above RITA.
explanation.definitionFit: This tequila cocktail with lime and a salted rim is a mixed alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Second bit of a pig required for game

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
gammon is cured meat from the hind leg of a pig

explanation.surface: A second cut of pork is needed for a meal, or perhaps for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' is the verb meaning support, not a unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: This board game for two players with dice and counters is one of the oldest known.

clue.text: Gain attention by end of audition

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of audition

explanation.surface: An actor wins notice by the close of their audition.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain money or credit through effort is the verb sense of this word.

clue.text: Take tea with outspoken member of the clergy

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
plain-spoken or blunt speech is plain

explanation.surface: Have a cuppa with a blunt-talking vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cleric attached to an institution such as a hospital, regiment or college.

clue.text: Page about super sort of dwelling

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
fab, short for fabulous, means super

explanation.surface: A page in a magazine features a wonderful kind of house.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory-built house assembled on site, common in post-war Britain, is a type of home.

clue.text: Hurt one squeezing hard

indicators.note: squeezing means pressing something in, so the hard letter goes inside

parts.note: an ace counts as one in cards and dice
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone is injured while gripping something hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurt in the sense of being sore or throbbing is to feel this dull pain.

clue.text: Self-control in school? Nothing certain

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive, the UK state secondary school for all abilities
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A question about whether discipline is taught at school, answered with certainty about nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Calmness and keeping one's feelings in check is self-possession, the sense here.

clue.text: Mocking foolish raids on clubs

indicators.note: foolish suggests something ill-judged and muddled, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at ill-advised police raids on nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Grimly scornful and derisive describes a sneering, cynical remark.

clue.text: In a risky situation in hot stormy French resort

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Trouble brews on the Riviera, sweltering and stormy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' turns IN HOT into ONTHI, completed by NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom pictures a skater on frozen water that may crack, meaning in a precarious position.

clue.text: I am interrupting to put off bore

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the I am letters go inside

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage

explanation.surface: Someone breaks in to discourage a tedious person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' is not a dull person but the width of a gun barrel or tube.
explanation.definitionFit: The bore of a pipe or barrel is its internal width, measured straight across.

clue.text: Oversight? Ring diplomatic office abroad

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O
an embassy or legation in a foreign country is a mission

explanation.surface: A slip-up: phone the embassy overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left out by mistake is a failure to notice, which is an oversight.

clue.text: Catch some returning

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for some is read backwards

parts.note: part means some, as in part of the cake

explanation.surface: Bring in a portion of the returning fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch an animal is to snare it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Credit is double in emergency

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: double means the word is given twice over

explanation.surface: Borrowing has doubled during an urgent situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A time of acute danger or difficulty needing urgent action is a critical moment.

clue.text: Bed? Saw bishop retiring

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a saw is a saying or maxim, like a motto
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop heads to bed, as a saw is put away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' sounds bedtime-like but reverses MOTTO B.
explanation.definitionFit: The seabed or riverbed is the floor beneath the water, its lowest surface.

clue.text: Complete wreck

definitions.meaning: complete as in utter or absolute, an adjective
to wreck a car beyond repair, an informal verb sense

explanation.definitionFit: The word means entire or absolute, and colloquially to write off a vehicle completely.

clue.text: Frank's poker hand

definitions.meaning: five cards in sequence form this hand in poker

explanation.surface: Frank, a man with cards, is holding a hand at poker.
explanation.definitionFit: Honest speaking is plain and direct, and a run of five consecutive cards beats three of a kind.

clue.text: Raise one in army

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one within the word for an army

parts.note: a host is an army or great multitude
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Promote a single soldier in the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something up, often with ropes or a crane, is this verb.

clue.text: Only fair? Quite fitting

definitions.meaning: only as in merely, an adverb
fair as in equitable and right
quite as in exactly, an adverb
fitting as in deserved or appropriate

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something is merely equitable and is told it is entirely appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means merely, equitable, exactly and deserved, four separate senses strung together.

clue.text: Fresh meat and brandy, say — it brings people together

indicators.note: fresh suggests something new, so the letters of meat are remade

parts.note: brandy is an example of a spirit

explanation.surface: New meat and a glass of brandy make a convivial meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like it describes the meat but signals the anagram TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A shared sense of unity and cooperation makes a group pull together.

clue.text: In good health, British cardinal, perhaps of good stock

parts.note: well means in good health
cardinal is a shade of red, the colour of a cardinal's robes

explanation.surface: A healthy British cardinal comes from a fine family.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming from a respectable, refined family is to have a good pedigree or upbringing.

clue.text: Detective let us out in front of hotel

indicators.note: out suggests something put wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A detective releases us in front of the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: An investigator who tracks down clues, originally a bloodhound following a trail, is a private eye.
